Read AudioMoth metadata from a wave file

Source: R/audiomoth.R
audiomothWave.Rd

Reads and parses metadata stored in wave files produced by AudioMoth devices.

Usage

audiomothWave(filename)

Arguments

filename

Path to the wave file to read

Value

A list of extracted parameters:

raw

The comment string the other fields were read from

start_time

Recording start time, as "HH:MM:SS"

start_date

Recording start date, as "DD/MM/YYYY"

time_zone

Time zone of the start time, e.g. "UTC" or "UTC+1"

serial

The device serial number, or NA for a deployment ID file

deployment_id

The configured deployment ID, or NA if none was set

gain

Gain setting, one of "low", "low-medium", "medium", "medium-high" or "high"

voltage

Battery voltage in volts. Where the firmware reported only that the battery was outside the range it measures, the threshold it compared against is returned with a leading "<" or ">", e.g. "<2.5". The thresholds themselves have changed: firmware up to 1.2.0 wrote "<3.6" and ">5.0", 1.2.2 and 1.3.0 "<3.6" and ">4.9", and 1.4.0 onwards "<2.5" and ">4.9"

temperature

Temperature in degrees Celsius, or NA for firmware before 1.4.0, which did not record it

external_mic

Whether an external microphone was used

filter

"Low-pass", "Band-pass", "High-pass", or FALSE if no filter was applied

filter.limit

Filter frequency in kHz, two values separated by a hyphen for a band-pass filter, or FALSE if no filter was applied

cancelled

Why the recording stopped early, or FALSE if it ran to completion

Details

The comment written into the wave header has been reworded several times across AudioMoth-Firmware-Basic releases, most significantly in 1.6.0, where "at medium gain setting while battery state was" became "at medium gain while battery was" and the filter and cancellation clauses were rephrased. Fields are matched by pattern rather than by position, so all wordings from 1.0 onwards are read.

Firmware from 1.5.0 can be configured with a deployment ID, which the firmware writes in place of the device serial number. Such files have a deployment_id and no serial.

Firmware before 1.4.0 wrote a gain index rather than a gain name, so gain is a number ("0" to "4") for files from those versions.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
audiomothWave("./FILENAME.WAV")
} # }
